------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m7p3t1 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, Slots, MaxVer, MaxSubs

VARIABLES
    held,       \* set of << controller, slot >> bindings currently in force
    ver,        \* [Slots -> Nat] : compare-and-swap version register per slot
    net,        \* set of in-flight bind requests [ctl, slot, exp]
    subs,       \* count of bind requests ever submitted (bounds the run)
    offline     \* set of controllers currently off the mesh

vars == << held, ver, net, subs, offline >>

Msg == [ctl: Controllers, slot: Slots, exp: 0..MaxVer]

SlotFree(s) == \A c \in Controllers : << c, s >> \notin held

TypeOK ==
    /\ held \subseteq (Controllers \X Slots)
    /\ ver \in [Slots -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ net \subseteq Msg
    /\ subs \in 0..MaxSubs
    /\ offline \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ held = {}
    /\ ver = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ net = {}
    /\ subs = 0
    /\ offline = {}

\* An online controller reads a slot's current version and puts a bind request
\* on the network; the mesh may deliver it much later, out of order.
Submit(c, s) ==
    /\ c \notin offline
    /\ subs < MaxSubs
    /\ subs' = subs + 1
    /\ net' = net \cup {[ctl |-> c, slot |-> s, exp |-> ver[s]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED << held, ver, offline >>

\* A delivered request binds the slot only if the slot is free AND its live
\* version still matches -- the compare-and-swap defeats stale reordered mail.
Deliver(m) ==
    /\ m \in net
    /\ SlotFree(m.slot)
    /\ ver[m.slot] = m.exp
    /\ ver[m.slot] < MaxVer
    /\ held' = held \cup {<< m.ctl, m.slot >>}
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![m.slot] = ver[m.slot] + 1]
    /\ net' = net \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED << subs, offline >>

\* A request that arrives stale (version moved, or slot already bound) is dropped.
DropStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in net
    /\ (ver[m.slot] # m.exp \/ ~SlotFree(m.slot))
    /\ net' = net \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED << held, ver, subs, offline >>

\* The owning controller releases the slot, bumping the version so no lingering
\* stale request can rebind against the old value.
Release(c, s) ==
    /\ << c, s >> \in held
    /\ ver[s] < MaxVer
    /\ held' = held \ {<< c, s >>}
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![s] = ver[s] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << net, subs, offline >>

\* A controller drops off the mesh (perpetually available: keeps the network
\* live and models flaky connectivity).
GoOffline(c) ==
    /\ c \notin offline
    /\ offline' = offline \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED << held, ver, net, subs >>

\* An offline controller rejoins the mesh.
ComeOnline(c) ==
    /\ c \in offline
    /\ offline' = offline \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED << held, ver, net, subs >>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, s \in Slots : Submit(c, s)
    \/ \E m \in net : Deliver(m)
    \/ \E m \in net : DropStale(m)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, s \in Slots : Release(c, s)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : GoOffline(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : ComeOnline(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a single slot is never held by two distinct
\* controllers at the same time.
NoDoubleBinding ==
    \A c1, c2 \in Controllers, s \in Slots :
        (<< c1, s >> \in held /\ << c2, s >> \in held) => c1 = c2

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    MaxVer = 3
    MaxSubs = 4

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT NoDoubleBinding
nl:
A smart-home hub manages a small bank of door-lock pairing slots that guest key-fobs bind to. Several controllers on the mesh network race to bind a fob to a free slot, and each slot carries a compare-and-swap register: a version number that must match for a bind to take effect. A controller first reads a slot's current version and then puts a bind request onto the network carrying that expected version; because the mesh delivers messages in any order, requests can arrive stale, long after another controller has already rebound the slot. When a bind request is delivered, the hub applies it only if the slot's live version still equals the expected version the request carried; a successful bind records the owning controller and bumps the slot version by one, so any other in-flight request that read the old version is now doomed to fail. A stale request whose expected version no longer matches is simply discarded. A controller may also release a slot it owns, which clears the owner and bumps the version again so no lingering request can revive the binding. Controllers can drop off the flaky mesh and rejoin it at any time; while offline a controller submits nothing, though requests it already sent may still arrive. The whole danger is that two controllers, both having read the same old version, could otherwise each believe they own the same slot at once. The compare-and-swap version guard is exactly what stops that second bind from taking hold.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No door-lock slot is ever simultaneously bound to two different controllers.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m5p2t0 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Total

VARIABLES
    bal,        \* [Nodes -> Nat] : access tokens held at each hub node
    pending,    \* TRUE iff a transfer proposal is open
    proposal,   \* the open transfer [from, to] (meaningful only when pending)
    votes,      \* set of nodes that have voted yes on the pending proposal
    crashed     \* set of nodes that have silently crashed

vars == << bal, pending, proposal, votes, crashed >>

RECURSIVE SumFn(_, _)
SumFn(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET n == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
         IN f[n] + SumFn(f, S \ {n})

Quorum(V) == Cardinality(V) * 2 > Cardinality(Nodes)

TypeOK ==
    /\ bal \in [Nodes -> 0..Total]
    /\ pending \in BOOLEAN
    /\ proposal \in [from: Nodes, to: Nodes]
    /\ votes \subseteq Nodes
    /\ crashed \subseteq Nodes

Init ==
    /\ bal \in {b \in [Nodes -> 0..Total] : SumFn(b, Nodes) = Total}
    /\ pending = FALSE
    /\ proposal = [from |-> CHOOSE x \in Nodes : TRUE,
                   to   |-> CHOOSE x \in Nodes : TRUE]
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

\* A live node opens a proposal to move one token from a source to a distinct
\* destination; whether the source holds a token is checked at commit.
Propose(a, b) ==
    /\ ~pending
    /\ a \notin crashed
    /\ a # b
    /\ pending' = TRUE
    /\ proposal' = [from |-> a, to |-> b]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED << bal, crashed >>

\* A live node casts a yes-vote on the open proposal.
Vote(n) ==
    /\ pending
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ n \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED << bal, pending, proposal, crashed >>

\* Once yes-votes reach a quorum, the transfer commits: exactly one token
\* leaves the source and arrives at the destination.
Commit ==
    /\ pending
    /\ Quorum(votes)
    /\ bal[proposal.from] > 0
    /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![proposal.from] = @ - 1,
                          ![proposal.to]   = @ + 1]
    /\ pending' = FALSE
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED << proposal, crashed >>

\* A proposal that cannot muster support is cleared.
Abort ==
    /\ pending
    /\ pending' = FALSE
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED << bal, proposal, crashed >>

\* At most one node crashes silently: it stops voting and never returns.
Crash(n) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
    /\ votes' = votes \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED << bal, pending, proposal >>

Next ==
    \/ \E a, b \in Nodes : Propose(a, b)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Vote(n)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: no vote, transfer, abort, or crash ever creates or destroys a
\* token -- the pool total is invariant.
TokenPoolConserved == SumFn(bal, Nodes) = Total

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
    Total = 2

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT TokenPoolConserved
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network shares a fixed pool of digital access tokens among several hub nodes; a token sitting at a node authorizes that node to open a door. Nodes redistribute tokens by transfer, but no transfer is unilateral: to move one token from a source node to a destination node, a quorum -- strictly more than half of the still-live nodes -- must vote to approve the pending proposal. A node proposes a transfer, other live nodes cast votes for it, and once the yes-votes form a quorum the transfer commits, decrementing the source's token count and incrementing the destination's. If a quorum cannot be gathered the proposal is aborted and cleared. A node can crash silently at any time: it simply stops voting and never returns, which only makes quorums harder to reach but must never conjure or destroy a token. Because every commit moves exactly one token from one balance to another, the grand total of tokens held across all nodes must stay fixed no matter how transfers, votes, aborts, and crashes interleave. The property at stake is pure conservation of the token pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of access tokens held across all hub nodes always equals the fixed pool size.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m7p1t5 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxVer

VARIABLES
    version,    \* live version number of the shared runway record
    lastBase,   \* the base version the most recent applied write was built on
    net,        \* set of submitted writes [w |-> controller, base |-> Nat]
    locked      \* TRUE while the supervisor holds the record for override

vars == << version, lastBase, net, locked >>

Write == [w: Controllers, base: 0..MaxVer]

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ lastBase \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ net \subseteq Write
    /\ locked \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ lastBase = 0
    /\ net = {}
    /\ locked = FALSE

\* A controller reads the live version and submits a write tagged with it.
Submit(c) ==
    /\ ~locked
    /\ net' = net \cup {[w |-> c, base |-> version]}
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, lastBase, locked >>

\* A submitted write applies only if its base still matches -- the compare-and-
\* swap rejects any write that another update has since overtaken.
Apply(m) ==
    /\ ~locked
    /\ m \in net
    /\ m.base = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ lastBase' = m.base
    /\ net' = net \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED locked

\* A write whose base no longer matches the live version is stale; discard it.
DropStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in net
    /\ m.base # version
    /\ net' = net \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, lastBase, locked >>

\* While holding the lock, the supervisor forces a write past the version check;
\* it still builds on the current version, keeping the update chain intact.
ForceWrite ==
    /\ locked
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ lastBase' = version
    /\ UNCHANGED << net, locked >>

\* The supervisor may take and release the override lock at any time.
Lock ==
    /\ ~locked
    /\ locked' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, lastBase, net >>

Unlock ==
    /\ locked
    /\ locked' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, lastBase, net >>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Submit(c)
    \/ \E m \in net : Apply(m)
    \/ \E m \in net : DropStale(m)
    \/ ForceWrite
    \/ Lock
    \/ Unlock

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the most recent applied write was based on the version that
\* immediately preceded it, so no write ever skipped over and discarded another.
NoLostUpdate == (version = 0) \/ (lastBase = version - 1)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    MaxVer = 3

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator keeps a single shared assignment record that says which flight currently owns the active runway. Several controllers update this record concurrently, but each guards its write with a compare-and-swap: a controller first reads the record's current version number, prepares a write tagged with that base version, and submits it. When a submitted write is applied, it takes effect only if its base version still equals the record's live version; a successful write advances the version by one and remembers the base it was built on. A write whose base no longer matches the live version is stale and is discarded rather than applied, because applying it would silently clobber an update another controller already made. A privileged supervisor can lock the record for a manual override and, while it is free to do so, force a write that bypasses the version check; the override still advances the version and records the base it built on, so it too leaves a clean update chain. The supervisor may lock and unlock the record at will. The hazard being guarded against is a lost update: a stale write overwriting a newer one so that the newer controller's assignment quietly disappears.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every applied update to the runway record is built on the version immediately preceding it, so no update is ever overwritten and lost.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m3p4t5 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Elevators, Cap, MaxCalls

VARIABLES
    load,       \* [Elevators -> Nat] : passengers currently in each cabin
    leader,     \* the dispatcher elevator, or "none"
    alive,      \* set of elevators currently in service
    calls       \* number of hall calls waiting to be served

vars == << load, leader, alive, calls >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in [Elevators -> 0..(Cap + 2)]
    /\ leader \in (Elevators \cup {"none"})
    /\ alive \subseteq Elevators
    /\ calls \in 0..MaxCalls

Init ==
    /\ load = [e \in Elevators |-> 0]
    /\ leader = "none"
    /\ alive = Elevators
    /\ calls = 0

\* A new hall call arrives and queues up.
Arrive ==
    /\ calls < MaxCalls
    /\ calls' = calls + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << load, leader, alive >>

\* The dispatcher lets a waiting passenger board an alive cabin below capacity.
Board(e) ==
    /\ leader \in alive
    /\ e \in alive
    /\ calls > 0
    /\ load[e] < Cap
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![e] = load[e] + 1]
    /\ calls' = calls - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, alive >>

\* A passenger exits a cabin.
Exit(e) ==
    /\ load[e] > 0
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![e] = load[e] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, alive, calls >>

\* When the dispatcher role is vacant (or its holder failed), elect an alive one.
Elect(e) ==
    /\ leader \notin alive
    /\ e \in alive
    /\ leader' = e
    /\ UNCHANGED << load, alive, calls >>

\* An elevator fails and drops out of service; a failed dispatcher role falls vacant.
Fail(e) ==
    /\ e \in alive
    /\ alive' = alive \ {e}
    /\ leader' = IF leader = e THEN "none" ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED << load, calls >>

\* A failed elevator returns to service.
Recover(e) ==
    /\ e \notin alive
    /\ alive' = alive \cup {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED << load, leader, calls >>

\* The administrator overrides the election, installing any alive dispatcher.
AdminSetLeader(e) ==
    /\ e \in alive
    /\ leader' = e
    /\ UNCHANGED << load, alive, calls >>

Next ==
    \/ Arrive
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Board(e)
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Exit(e)
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Elect(e)
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Fail(e)
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Recover(e)
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : AdminSetLeader(e)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: every cabin's load stays within its fixed capacity.
CapacityRespected == \A e \in Elevators : load[e] <= Cap

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Elevators = {e1, e2}
    Cap = 2
    MaxCalls = 3

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A bank of elevators in a skyscraper is coordinated by a single dispatcher role held by one elevator's controller, elected among the currently alive elevators. Hall calls arrive and queue up; the dispatcher authorizes a waiting passenger to board a specific alive elevator, but only if that elevator is below its cabin capacity. Boarding moves one waiting passenger into the cabin and raises that cabin's load by one; passengers also exit, lowering a cabin's load. An elevator can fail and drop out of service, and if the failed one was the dispatcher the role falls vacant; any alive elevator can then be elected to fill the vacant dispatcher role (failover). Failed elevators can be recovered back into service. A privileged building administrator may override the election and install any alive elevator as dispatcher immediately. No matter how calls arrive, how boarding and exits interleave, or how the dispatcher role fails over and gets overridden, a cabin's load must never rise above its fixed capacity. The capacity guard on boarding is what protects this bound.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No elevator cabin ever holds more passengers than its fixed capacity.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m6p6t5 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Bays, Workers, LeaseDur, MaxClock

VARIABLES
    clock,      \* shared monotonic clock
    holder,     \* [Bays -> Workers \cup {"free"}] : current lease holder
    expiry,     \* [Bays -> Nat] : clock time at which each bay's lease expires
    busy,       \* [Bays -> BOOLEAN] : whether a wash is in progress
    operator    \* [Bays -> Workers \cup {"free"}] : worker running the wash

vars == << clock, holder, expiry, busy, operator >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ holder \in [Bays -> Workers \cup {"free"}]
    /\ expiry \in [Bays -> 0..(MaxClock + LeaseDur)]
    /\ busy \in [Bays -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ operator \in [Bays -> Workers \cup {"free"}]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ holder = [b \in Bays |-> "free"]
    /\ expiry = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ busy = [b \in Bays |-> FALSE]
    /\ operator = [b \in Bays |-> "free"]

\* A worker acquires the lease of a currently free bay.
Acquire(b, w) ==
    /\ holder[b] = "free"
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = w]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![b] = clock + LeaseDur]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, busy, operator >>

\* Only the current holder, with a live lease, may start a wash on the bay.
Start(b, w) ==
    /\ holder[b] = w
    /\ clock < expiry[b]
    /\ ~busy[b]
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ operator' = [operator EXCEPT ![b] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, holder, expiry >>

\* A wash finishes.
Finish(b) ==
    /\ busy[b]
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ operator' = [operator EXCEPT ![b] = "free"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, holder, expiry >>

\* Time advances.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, expiry, busy, operator >>

\* An expired lease is reclaimed: the holder is cleared and any wash aborted.
Expire(b) ==
    /\ holder[b] # "free"
    /\ clock >= expiry[b]
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = "free"]
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ operator' = [operator EXCEPT ![b] = "free"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, expiry >>

\* The administrator overrides the lease, handing the bay to any worker and
\* preempting whatever wash was in progress.
AdminAssign(b, w) ==
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = w]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![b] = clock + LeaseDur]
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ operator' = [operator EXCEPT ![b] = "free"]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bays, w \in Workers : Acquire(b, w)
    \/ \E b \in Bays, w \in Workers : Start(b, w)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Finish(b)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Expire(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bays, w \in Workers : AdminAssign(b, w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized or stale operation: a bay under wash is always driven by
\* precisely its current lease holder.
OnlyHolderOperates ==
    \A b \in Bays : busy[b] => (operator[b] = holder[b])

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bays = {b1, b2}
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    LeaseDur = 2
    MaxClock = 3

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT OnlyHolderOperates
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has several wash bays, each of which is operated by at most one crew worker at a time under a time-limited lease. To operate a bay a worker must first acquire the bay's lease, which names that worker as holder and sets an expiry time measured against a shared clock. Only the bay's current lease holder may start a wash on that bay, and only while the lease has not yet expired; starting a wash marks the bay busy and records the operating worker. A wash finishes, clearing the busy mark. The shared clock ticks forward, and when a bay's lease expires the bay is reclaimed: its holder is cleared and any wash in progress is aborted, since a worker whose lease lapsed has no authority to keep operating. A privileged site administrator may override the lease and hand a bay to any worker immediately, which preempts and clears any wash currently in progress. The whole point of the lease discipline is that a bay is never operated by anyone other than its current authorized holder: no stale or unauthorized worker ever drives a bay. The holder check on starting a wash is what enforces this.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a bay is being washed, the worker operating it is exactly that bay's current lease holder.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m6p5t5 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Slots, Controllers, LeaseDur, MaxClock

VARIABLES
    clock,      \* shared monotonic clock
    holder,     \* [Slots -> Controllers \cup {"free"}] : current lease holder
    expiry,     \* [Slots -> Nat] : clock time each slot's lease expires
    vended,     \* [Slots -> BOOLEAN] : whether the slot has been vended
    vcount      \* [Slots -> Nat] : number of times the slot was vended

vars == << clock, holder, expiry, vended, vcount >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ holder \in [Slots -> Controllers \cup {"free"}]
    /\ expiry \in [Slots -> 0..(MaxClock + LeaseDur)]
    /\ vended \in [Slots -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ vcount \in [Slots -> 0..2]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ holder = [s \in Slots |-> "free"]
    /\ expiry = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ vended = [s \in Slots |-> FALSE]
    /\ vcount = [s \in Slots |-> 0]

\* A controller leases a currently free slot.
Acquire(s, c) ==
    /\ holder[s] = "free"
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = clock + LeaseDur]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, vended, vcount >>

\* The holder vends the slot -- once only -- while its lease is live.
Vend(s, c) ==
    /\ holder[s] = c
    /\ clock < expiry[s]
    /\ ~vended[s]
    /\ vended' = [vended EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ vcount' = [vcount EXCEPT ![s] = vcount[s] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, holder, expiry >>

\* Time advances.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, expiry, vended, vcount >>

\* An expired lease is reclaimed, freeing the slot to be leased again.
Expire(s) ==
    /\ holder[s] # "free"
    /\ clock >= expiry[s]
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = "free"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, expiry, vended, vcount >>

\* The administrator overrides the lease, handing the slot to any controller.
AdminAssign(s, c) ==
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = clock + LeaseDur]
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, vended, vcount >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots, c \in Controllers : Acquire(s, c)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, c \in Controllers : Vend(s, c)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Expire(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, c \in Controllers : AdminAssign(s, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Irreversible vend happens at most once: the vend count of a slot is exactly
\* one when it has been vended and zero when it has not.
VendedAtMostOnce ==
    \A s \in Slots : vcount[s] = (IF vended[s] THEN 1 ELSE 0)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    LeaseDur = 2
    MaxClock = 3

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT VendedAtMostOnce
nl:
A network of vending machines exposes a set of product slots, each of which can be vended exactly once because vending both dispenses the physical item and charges the customer -- an irreversible act. Route controllers service the machines, and to vend a slot a controller must hold a time-limited lease on that slot: the lease names the controller as holder and carries an expiry against a shared clock. A controller may vend a slot only while it holds a live lease and only if the slot has not already been vended; a vend marks the slot vended and bumps that slot's vend counter. The clock ticks forward, and an expired lease is reclaimed so the slot becomes free to lease again. A privileged operations administrator may override the lease and reassign a slot's holder to any controller at once. Crucially, no matter how leases are acquired, expire, or get overridden, the physical vend of a slot must happen at most once: the slot's vend count is one exactly when it has been vended and zero otherwise, never two. The already-vended guard is what makes the irreversible vend fire at most once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Each product slot is vended at most once -- its recorded vend count is one when vended and zero otherwise.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m2p5t3 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Sites

VARIABLES
    vote,       \* [Sites -> {"none","yes","no"}] : each site's prepare vote
    decision,   \* "none" | "commit" | "abort" : the final global decision
    released,   \* number of times the units were physically released
    slow        \* set of sites currently slow (deferring their vote)

vars == << vote, decision, released, slow >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ vote \in [Sites -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ decision \in {"none", "commit", "abort"}
    /\ released \in 0..2
    /\ slow \subseteq Sites

Init ==
    /\ vote = [s \in Sites |-> "none"]

\* commit decision that was reached under unanimous yes votes.

    /\ released <= 1
    /\ (released = 1 => decision = "commit")
    /\ (decision = "commit" => \A s \in Sites : vote[s] = "yes")

    fine,       \* [Slots -> Threads \cup {"free"}] : per-slot fine lock
    pool,       \* set of settlement slots still available in the shared pool
    alloc       \* set of << thread, slot >> committed allocations

    /\ fine \in [Slots -> Threads \cup {"free"}]

    /\ alloc \subseteq (Threads \X Slots)

    /\ fine = [s \in Slots |-> "free"]
    /\ pool = Slots
    /\ alloc = {}

AcquireCoarse(t) ==
    /\ coarse[Engine(t)] = "free"
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![Engine(t)] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, pool, alloc >>

\* Only while holding the coarse lock may a thread take a slot's fine lock.
AcquireFine(t, s) ==
    /\ coarse[Engine(t)] = t
    /\ fine[s] = "free"
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, pool, alloc >>

\* shared pool exactly once and recording the allocation.
Allocate(t, s) ==
    /\ fine[s] = t
    /\ s \in pool
    /\ pool' = pool \ {s}
    /\ alloc' = alloc \cup {<< t, s >>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine >>

\* A thread drops a slot's fine lock.
ReleaseFine(t, s) ==
    /\ fine[s] = t
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = "free"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, pool, alloc >>

\* A thread drops its engine's coarse book lock.
ReleaseCoarse(t) ==
    /\ coarse[Engine(t)] = t
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![Engine(t)] = "free"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, pool, alloc >>

    \/ \E t \in Threads : AcquireCoarse(t)
    \/ \E t \in Threads, s \in Slots : AcquireFine(t, s)
    \/ \E t \in Threads, s \in Slots : Allocate(t, s)
    \/ \E t \in Threads, s \in Slots : ReleaseFine(t, s)

\* threads.

A bank runs its overnight interbank settlement as a batch, and two independent settlement engines (instance A and instance B) draw settlement slots from one shared pool. Each engine has its own worker threads. To claim a slot a thread must respect a two-level lock hierarchy: it first acquires its engine's coarse book lock, and only while holding that coarse lock may it acquire the fine lock on an individual slot. A thread holding a slot's fine lock may then allocate the slot, which removes it from the shared pool and records the allocation to that thread. Fine locks are released, and coarse book locks are released, so threads and engines keep cycling. Because the two engines share one pool, the real hazard is a slot being allocated to two different threads -- a double settlement of the same obligation. The fine lock is exclusive per slot and the slot is drawn from the shared pool exactly once, so once a slot leaves the pool no other thread can allocate it. The safety concern is strictly that no settlement slot is ever allocated to two different threads.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No settlement slot is ever allocated to two different threads.

    net,        \* set of trains whose entry requests are in flight (reorderable)
    occ         \* current occupancy count of the holding block

Request(t) ==

    /\ t \notin net
    /\ net' = net \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, inBlock, leaseExp, occ >>

\* The dispatcher grants a train a fresh time-limited movement authority.
Grant(t) ==

    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, inBlock, net, occ >>

    /\ clock < leaseExp[t]
    /\ ~inBlock[t]

    /\ net' = net \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, leaseExp >>

    /\ inBlock' = [inBlock EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ occ' = occ - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, leaseExp, net >>

    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << inBlock, leaseExp, net, occ >>

DropStale(t) ==
    /\ t \in net
    /\ clock >= leaseExp[t]
    /\ net' = net \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, inBlock, leaseExp, occ >>

    \/ \E t \in Trains : Grant(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Enter(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Exit(t)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E t \in Trains : DropStale(t)

    operating,  \* [Rooms -> Teams \cup {"none"}] : team currently operating
    opEpoch     \* [Rooms -> Nat] : epoch each in-progress operation started under

Assign(r, tm) ==

    free,       \* free capacity tokens remaining in the shared pool
    out,        \* [Instances -> Nat] : outstanding jobs per dispatcher
    mode        \* [Instances -> {"run","paused"}] : backpressure state

    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![i] = "run"]

    holder,     \* [Locks -> Users \cup {"none"}] : current lease holder
    gen,        \* [Locks -> Nat] : lease generation, bumped each acquisition
    acting,     \* [Locks -> Users \cup {"none"}] : user mid-unlock
    actGen      \* [Locks -> Nat] : generation the in-progress unlock started under

NumActive == Cardinality({l \in Locks : holder[l] # "none"})

    /\ holder \in [Locks -> Users \cup {"none"}]
    /\ gen \in [Locks -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ acting \in [Locks -> Users \cup {"none"}]
    /\ actGen \in [Locks -> 0..MaxGen]

Init ==
    /\ cap = 1
    /\ holder = [l \in Locks |-> "none"]
    /\ gen = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ acting = [l \in Locks |-> "none"]
    /\ actGen = [l \in Locks |-> 0]

\* A user leases an unleased lock if capacity allows; the generation bumps.
Acquire(l, u) ==
    /\ holder[l] = "none"
    /\ NumActive < cap
    /\ gen[l] < MaxGen
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![l] = u]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![l] = gen[l] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << cap, acting, actGen >>

\* Only the current holder may start an unlock; it is stamped with the generation.
Unlock(l, u) ==
    /\ holder[l] = u
    /\ acting[l] = "none"
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![l] = u]
    /\ actGen' = [actGen EXCEPT ![l] = gen[l]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << cap, holder, gen >>

\* An unlock completes.
Finish(l) ==
    /\ acting[l] # "none"
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![l] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << cap, holder, gen, actGen >>

\* The holder voluntarily releases the lease when no unlock is in progress.
Release(l) ==
    /\ holder[l] # "none"
    /\ acting[l] = "none"
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![l] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << cap, gen, acting, actGen >>

\* The hub revokes a lock's lease, aborting any unlock in progress.
Revoke(l) ==
    /\ holder[l] # "none"
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![l] = "none"]
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![l] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << cap, gen, actGen >>

\* Runtime capacity changes.
RaiseCap ==
    /\ cap < MaxCap
    /\ cap' = cap + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, gen, acting, actGen >>

LowerCap ==
    /\ cap > 1
    /\ cap' = cap - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, gen, acting, actGen >>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Locks, u \in Users : Acquire(l, u)
    \/ \E l \in Locks, u \in Users : Unlock(l, u)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Finish(l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Release(l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Revoke(l)
    \/ RaiseCap
    \/ LowerCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized or stale operation: an unlock in progress is driven by the
\* lock's current holder under its current lease generation.
OnlyHolderActs ==
    \A l \in Locks :
        acting[l] # "none" =>
            (acting[l] = holder[l] /\ actGen[l] = gen[l])

------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m0p0t5 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Workers, MaxVer

VARIABLES
    owner,      \* current owner of the wash tunnel, or "none"
    inCS,       \* [Workers -> BOOLEAN] : whether each worker is inside the tunnel
    version,    \* lock version of the tunnel
    snap        \* [Workers -> Nat] : each worker's optimistic version snapshot

vars == << owner, inCS, version, snap >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Workers \cup {"none"}
    /\ inCS \in [Workers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ snap \in [Workers -> 0..MaxVer]

Init ==
    /\ owner = "none"
    /\ inCS = [w \in Workers |-> FALSE]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ snap = [w \in Workers |-> 0]

\* A worker optimistically reads the tunnel's current version.
Read(w) ==
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![w] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, inCS, version >>

\* Entry commits only if the version is unchanged and the tunnel is unowned.
Enter(w) ==
    /\ version = snap[w]
    /\ owner = "none"
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = w
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![w] = TRUE]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* A worker whose snapshot went stale re-reads and retries.
Retry(w) ==
    /\ version # snap[w]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![w] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, inCS, version >>

\* A worker leaves the tunnel, releasing ownership.
Leave(w) ==
    /\ inCS[w]
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = "none"
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![w] = FALSE]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* The administrator forces a worker into the tunnel, preempting all others.
AdminGrant(w) ==
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = w
    /\ inCS' = [x \in Workers |-> x = w]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Read(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Enter(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Retry(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Leave(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : AdminGrant(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion: any worker inside the tunnel must be the single owner, so
\* two workers are never inside at once.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A w \in Workers : inCS[w] => (owner = w)

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2, w3}
    MaxVer = 4

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has a single wash tunnel that is a critical resource: at most one crew worker may be inside operating it at any time. Access is coordinated by optimistic locking with retry. Each worker first reads the tunnel's lock version into a private snapshot, then optimistically attempts to enter. An entry commits only if the version still equals the worker's snapshot and the tunnel is currently unowned; a successful entry marks the worker as owner, puts it inside, and bumps the version so every other worker's snapshot is now stale. A worker whose snapshot has gone stale simply re-reads the current version and retries. A worker leaves the tunnel, releasing ownership and bumping the version again. A privileged site administrator may override everything and force a specific worker into the tunnel, preempting anyone inside and leaving that worker as the sole occupant. The safety concern is strict mutual exclusion: the tunnel is never occupied by two workers at once. The unowned-and-version-matched guard on entry is what preserves this.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The wash tunnel is never occupied by more than one worker at a time.

CONSTANTS N, NumTokens

Nodes == 0 .. (N - 1)
Succ(n) == (n + 1) % N

VARIABLES
    atNode,     \* [Nodes -> Nat] : tokens resting at each node
    transit,    \* [Nodes -> Nat] : tokens in transit toward each node
    serving     \* [Nodes -> BOOLEAN] : whether a node is serving a train

vars == << atNode, transit, serving >>

RECURSIVE SumFn(_, _)
SumFn(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET n == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
         IN f[n] + SumFn(f, S \ {n})

TypeOK ==
    /\ atNode \in [Nodes -> 0..NumTokens]
    /\ transit \in [Nodes -> 0..NumTokens]
    /\ serving \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ atNode = [n \in Nodes |-> IF n = 0 THEN NumTokens ELSE 0]
    /\ transit = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ serving = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]

\* A node passes a resting token to its ring successor; it is now in transit.
Send(n) ==
    /\ atNode[n] > 0
    /\ atNode' = [atNode EXCEPT ![n] = atNode[n] - 1]
    /\ transit' = [transit EXCEPT ![Succ(n)] = transit[Succ(n)] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED serving

\* A token in transit toward node d is received and comes to rest there; transit
\* tokens may be received in any order.
Recv(d) ==
    /\ transit[d] > 0
    /\ transit' = [transit EXCEPT ![d] = transit[d] - 1]
    /\ atNode' = [atNode EXCEPT ![d] = atNode[d] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED serving

\* A token-holding node begins serving a train (exclusive access).
Use(n) ==
    /\ atNode[n] > 0
    /\ ~serving[n]
    /\ serving' = [serving EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << atNode, transit >>

\* A node finishes serving.
Done(n) ==
    /\ serving[n]
    /\ serving' = [serving EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << atNode, transit >>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Send(n)
    \/ \E d \in Nodes : Recv(d)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Use(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Done(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: resting tokens plus in-transit tokens always sum to the fixed
\* token count -- none is ever created or destroyed.
TokenConservation ==
    SumFn(atNode, Nodes) + SumFn(transit, Nodes) = NumTokens

A subway signalling system grants exclusive track access using a token ring: a fixed number of movement tokens circulate around a ring of signalling nodes, and a node may grant a train exclusive access only while it physically holds a token. Nodes pass tokens around the ring by sending a token to their ring successor, at which point the token is in transit; the successor later receives it and the token comes to rest there. Because the underlying links can reorder traffic, tokens in transit toward different nodes may be received in any order. A node holding a token can begin serving a train (exclusive access) and later finish serving. The one invariant that must hold no matter how tokens are passed, received in any order, or used to serve trains is conservation: the total number of tokens -- those resting at nodes plus those in transit -- is fixed forever, with none created and none destroyed. The paired decrement-on-send and increment-on-receive is what conserves the token count.

    ship,       \* [Stations -> Nat] : pills in transit toward each station
    dispensed,  \* total pills already dispensed to patients
    token       \* the ring position of the single dispensing token

    /\ stock \in [Stations -> 0..Total]
    /\ ship \in [Stations -> 0..Total]
    /\ dispensed \in 0..Total

    /\ ship = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ token = 0

Ship(s) ==
    /\ stock[s] > 0
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![s] = stock[s] - 1]
    /\ ship' = [ship EXCEPT ![Succ(s)] = ship[Succ(s)] + 1]

\* pills may be delivered in any order.

    /\ ship[d] > 0
    /\ ship' = [ship EXCEPT ![d] = ship[d] - 1]
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![d] = stock[d] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << dispensed, token >>

    /\ stock[s] > 0
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![s] = stock[s] - 1]
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << ship, token >>

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = Succ(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED << stock, ship, dispensed >>

    \/ \E d \in Stations : Deliver(d)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Dispense(s)
    \/ PassToken

\* fixed initial stock -- none created, none destroyed.
PillConservation ==
    SumFn(stock, Stations) + SumFn(ship, Stations) + dispensed = Total

A pharmacy prescription dispenser is organized as a ring of filling stations that share a fixed stock of pills. Exactly one dispensing token circulates around the ring, and only the station currently holding the token may dispense a pill to a patient. Stations also rebalance stock: a station ships one pill to its ring successor, putting that pill in transit, and the successor later takes delivery, moving the pill back into resting stock. Because shipments across the ring can be delivered in any order, in-transit pills bound for different stations need not arrive in the order they were sent. When the token-holding station dispenses, one pill leaves resting stock and is counted in the global dispensed tally. The token advances around the ring independently. ------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m2p6t4 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Subs, MaxRound, MaxCap

VARIABLES
    round,      \* current round number
    phase,      \* "idle" | "voting" | "committed"
    authRound,  \* [Subs -> Nat] : round each substation is authorized for (0 = none)
    applied,    \* [Subs -> Nat] : round each substation last applied under (0 = none)
    cap         \* runtime capacity: max substations that may shed this round

vars == << round, phase, authRound, applied, cap >>

NumAuth == Cardinality({s \in Subs : authRound[s] # 0})

TypeOK ==
    /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting", "committed"}
    /\ authRound \in [Subs -> 0..MaxRound]
    /\ applied \in [Subs -> 0..MaxRound]
    /\ cap \in 1..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ round = 0
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ authRound = [s \in Subs |-> 0]
    /\ applied = [s \in Subs |-> 0]
    /\ cap = 1

\* Open a new round: advance the round number and clear prior authorizations.
StartRound ==
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "committed"}
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ authRound' = [s \in Subs |-> 0]
    /\ applied' = [s \in Subs |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED cap

\* Authorize a substation to shed this round, within the current capacity.
Authorize(s) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ authRound[s] = 0
    /\ NumAuth < cap
    /\ authRound' = [authRound EXCEPT ![s] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, phase, applied, cap >>

\* Commit the round.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, authRound, applied, cap >>

\* A substation applies its shed only under a current-round authorization.
Apply(s) ==
    /\ phase = "committed"
    /\ authRound[s] = round
    /\ applied[s] = 0
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![s] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, phase, authRound, cap >>

\* Runtime capacity changes.
RaiseCap ==
    /\ cap < MaxCap
    /\ cap' = cap + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, phase, authRound, applied >>

LowerCap ==
    /\ cap > 1
    /\ cap' = cap - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << round, phase, authRound, applied >>

Next ==
    \/ StartRound
    \/ \E s \in Subs : Authorize(s)
    \/ Commit
    \/ \E s \in Subs : Apply(s)
    \/ RaiseCap
    \/ LowerCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized or stale action: any applied shed matches the substation's
\* current-round authorization.
AppliedMatchesAuth ==
    \A s \in Subs : applied[s] # 0 => applied[s] = authRound[s]

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Subs = {s1, s2, s3}
    MaxRound = 3
    MaxCap = 2

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT AppliedMatchesAuth
nl:
A power-grid load shedder coordinates emergency load-shedding across substations using two-phase commit, run in numbered rounds. To start a round the coordinator opens voting, advances the round number, and clears all prior authorizations and applied sheds. During voting the coordinator authorizes individual substations to shed, but only up to the current runtime capacity -- the maximum number of substations allowed to shed, which can be raised or lowered at runtime as grid conditions change. Once authorization is done the coordinator commits the round. A substation may then apply its shed, but only if it holds an authorization stamped with the current round; applying records the round under which it acted. A substation carrying only a stale authorization from an earlier round, or no authorization at all, has no authority and must not apply. The safety concern is that no substation ever applies a shed except under an authorization matching the very round it applied in: whenever a substation has applied, its recorded application round equals its current authorization round. The current-round authorization check on applying is what prevents any unauthorized or stale substation from acting.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every substation that has applied a load-shed did so under an authorization stamped with the same round it recorded applying in.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m0p3t1 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, Slots, MaxVer

VARIABLES
    alloc,      \* set of << crane, slot >> committed allocations
    gver,       \* single global version of the assignment table
    net,        \* set of in-flight claims [crane, slot, base]
    snap        \* [Cranes -> Nat] : each crane's last read of the global version

vars == << alloc, gver, net, snap >>

Claim == [crane: Cranes, slot: Slots, base: 0..MaxVer]

SlotFree(s) == \A c \in Cranes : << c, s >> \notin alloc

TypeOK ==
    /\ alloc \subseteq (Cranes \X Slots)
    /\ gver \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ net \subseteq Claim
    /\ snap \in [Cranes -> 0..MaxVer]

Init ==
    /\ alloc = {}
    /\ gver = 0
    /\ net = {}
    /\ snap = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]

\* A crane reads the current global version into its snapshot.
ReadVer(c) ==
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = gver]
    /\ UNCHANGED << alloc, gver, net >>

\* A crane submits a claim tagged with its snapshot; delivery may be reordered.
Submit(c, s) ==
    /\ net' = net \cup {[crane |-> c, slot |-> s, base |-> snap[c]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED << alloc, gver, snap >>

\* A claim commits only if its tag still matches and the slot is free; committing
\* bumps the global version, staling every other outstanding claim.
Commit(m) ==
    /\ m \in net
    /\ m.base = gver
    /\ SlotFree(m.slot)
    /\ gver < MaxVer
    /\ alloc' = alloc \cup {<< m.crane, m.slot >>}
    /\ gver' = gver + 1
    /\ net' = net \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* A claim whose tag no longer matches is stale and rejected (crane will retry).
Retry(m) ==
    /\ m \in net
    /\ m.base # gver
    /\ net' = net \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED << alloc, gver, snap >>

\* A crane releases a slot it owns, bumping the global version.
Release(c, s) ==
    /\ << c, s >> \in alloc
    /\ gver < MaxVer
    /\ alloc' = alloc \ {<< c, s >>}
    /\ gver' = gver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << net, snap >>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : ReadVer(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes, s \in Slots : Submit(c, s)
    \/ \E m \in net : Commit(m)
    \/ \E m \in net : Retry(m)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes, s \in Slots : Release(c, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a yard slot is never allocated to two distinct cranes.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A s \in Slots :
        \A c1, c2 \in Cranes :
            (<< c1, s >> \in alloc /\ << c2, s >> \in alloc) => c1 = c2

=============================================================================

    Cranes = {k1, k2}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    MaxVer = 3

INIT Init
NEXT Next

A container-ship crane yard assigns arriving containers to yard slots, with several cranes claiming slots concurrently under optimistic locking with retry. The whole assignment table carries a single global version number. A crane reads that version into a private snapshot, then submits a claim for a slot tagged with the snapshot it read; because the yard's control links can reorder traffic, claims arrive in arbitrary order. A submitted claim commits only if its tagged version still equals the table's live global version and the target slot is currently unallocated; committing records the crane as owner of that slot and bumps the global version, so every other outstanding claim tagged with the old version is now stale. A claim whose tag no longer matches the live version is rejected, and the crane must re-read the version and resubmit (retry). A crane may release a slot it owns, which also bumps the version. Because cranes race and claims are reordered, the safety concern is strictly that no yard slot is ever allocated to two different cranes. The version-match-and-slot-free guard on commit is what prevents any double allocation.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No yard slot is ever allocated to two different cranes.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Students, Seats, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES
    epoch,      \* current registration epoch
    pool,       \* set of seats free in the pool
    alloc,      \* set of << student, seat >> allocations
    claimEpoch  \* [Seats -> Nat] : epoch each held seat was claimed (0 = free)

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ pool \subseteq Seats
    /\ alloc \subseteq (Students \X Seats)
    /\ claimEpoch \in [Seats -> 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ pool = Seats
    /\ alloc = {}
    /\ claimEpoch = [se \in Seats |-> 0]

\* A student claims a free seat within the current epoch.
Claim(st, se) ==
    /\ se \in pool
    /\ pool' = pool \ {se}
    /\ alloc' = alloc \cup {<< st, se >>}
    /\ claimEpoch' = [claimEpoch EXCEPT ![se] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A student drops a seat, returning it to the pool.
Drop(st, se) ==
    /\ << st, se >> \in alloc
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {se}
    /\ alloc' = alloc \ {<< st, se >>}
    /\ claimEpoch' = [claimEpoch EXCEPT ![se] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Reconfig ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ pool' = Seats
    /\ alloc' = {}
    /\ claimEpoch' = [se \in Seats |-> 0]

\* The administrator force-assigns a seat, first removing any current holder so
\* the seat ends up held by exactly one student.
AdminAssign(st, se) ==
    /\ LET others == {p \in alloc : p[2] # se}
       IN alloc' = others \cup {<< st, se >>}
    /\ pool' = pool \ {se}
    /\ claimEpoch' = [claimEpoch EXCEPT ![se] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Next ==
    \/ \E st \in Students, se \in Seats : Claim(st, se)
    \/ \E st \in Students, se \in Seats : Drop(st, se)
    \/ Reconfig
    \/ \E st \in Students, se \in Seats : AdminAssign(st, se)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a seat is never allocated to two distinct students.
NoDoubleSeat ==
    \A se \in Seats :
        \A s1, s2 \in Students :
            (<< s1, se >> \in alloc /\ << s2, se >> \in alloc) => s1 = s2

A university course-registration system allocates a pool of course seats to students, and it runs in numbered registration epochs. Across all of this -- claims, drops, epoch reconfigurations, and admin overrides -- the safety concern is strictly that no course seat is ever allocated to two different students at once. The free-pool check on claiming, and the single-owner discipline of the override, are what prevent any double allocation.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m8p3t3 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Threads, Drawers, CabinetA, CabinetB

Cabinets == {"cA", "cB"}
CabOf(d) == IF d \in CabinetA THEN "cA" ELSE "cB"

VARIABLES
    cabLock,    \* [Cabinets -> Threads \cup {"free"}] : coarse cabinet lock
    drawerLock, \* [Drawers -> Threads \cup {"free"}] : fine drawer lock
    alloc,      \* set of << thread, drawer >> dispensations
    slow        \* set of threads currently slow (deferring)

vars == << cabLock, drawerLock, alloc, slow >>

DrawerFree(d) == \A t \in Threads : << t, d >> \notin alloc

TypeOK ==
    /\ cabLock \in [Cabinets -> Threads \cup {"free"}]
    /\ drawerLock \in [Drawers -> Threads \cup {"free"}]
    /\ alloc \subseteq (Threads \X Drawers)
    /\ slow \subseteq Threads

Init ==
    /\ cabLock = [c \in Cabinets |-> "free"]
    /\ drawerLock = [d \in Drawers |-> "free"]
    /\ alloc = {}
    /\ slow = {}

\* A non-slow thread takes the coarse lock on a cabinet (level one).
AcquireCab(t, c) ==
    /\ t \notin slow
    /\ cabLock[c] = "free"
    /\ cabLock' = [cabLock EXCEPT ![c] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED << drawerLock, alloc, slow >>

\* Only while holding the enclosing cabinet lock may a thread take a drawer lock.
AcquireDrawer(t, d) ==
    /\ t \notin slow
    /\ cabLock[CabOf(d)] = t
    /\ drawerLock[d] = "free"
    /\ drawerLock' = [drawerLock EXCEPT ![d] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED << cabLock, alloc, slow >>

\* Holding the drawer lock, the thread dispenses, allocating the drawer to it.
Dispense(t, d) ==
    /\ t \notin slow
    /\ drawerLock[d] = t
    /\ DrawerFree(d)
    /\ alloc' = alloc \cup {<< t, d >>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << cabLock, drawerLock, slow >>

\* A thread releases a drawer's fine lock.
ReleaseDrawer(t, d) ==
    /\ drawerLock[d] = t
    /\ drawerLock' = [drawerLock EXCEPT ![d] = "free"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << cabLock, alloc, slow >>

\* A thread releases a cabinet's coarse lock.
ReleaseCab(t, c) ==
    /\ cabLock[c] = t
    /\ cabLock' = [cabLock EXCEPT ![c] = "free"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << drawerLock, alloc, slow >>

\* A thread becomes slow (defers) or catches up -- it never fails.
BecomeSlow(t) ==
    /\ t \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED << cabLock, drawerLock, alloc >>

CatchUp(t) ==
    /\ t \in slow
    /\ slow' = slow \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED << cabLock, drawerLock, alloc >>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Threads, c \in Cabinets : AcquireCab(t, c)
    \/ \E t \in Threads, d \in Drawers : AcquireDrawer(t, d)
    \/ \E t \in Threads, d \in Drawers : Dispense(t, d)
    \/ \E t \in Threads, d \in Drawers : ReleaseDrawer(t, d)
    \/ \E t \in Threads, c \in Cabinets : ReleaseCab(t, c)
    \/ \E t \in Threads : BecomeSlow(t)
    \/ \E t \in Threads : CatchUp(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a drawer is never allocated to two distinct threads.
NoDoubleDrawer ==
    \A d \in Drawers :
        \A t1, t2 \in Threads :
            (<< t1, d >> \in alloc /\ << t2, d >> \in alloc) => t1 = t2

nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser stores medication in drawers grouped into cabinets, and dispenser threads pick items under a two-level lock hierarchy. To dispense from a drawer a thread must first take the coarse lock on the drawer's enclosing cabinet, and only while holding that cabinet lock may it take the fine lock on the individual drawer. Holding a drawer's fine lock, the thread may dispense from that drawer, which records the drawer as allocated to that thread; a drawer is dispensed from at most once. Fine drawer locks and coarse cabinet locks are both released so threads keep cycling through cabinets. A thread can be slow -- it may defer its next step for a while -- but it never fails outright, so it always eventually proceeds; a slow thread simply does not take new actions until it catches up. The safety concern is that no drawer is ever allocated to two different threads: two threads must never both dispense from the same drawer. The fine drawer lock, reachable only through the cabinet lock, together with the already-allocated guard, is what prevents any double allocation.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No drawer is ever allocated to two different dispenser threads.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m0p1t4 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Workers, MaxVer, MaxCap

VARIABLES
    version,    \* live version of the shared program record
    lastBase,   \* snapshot the most recent committed update was built on
    snap,       \* [Workers -> Nat] : each worker's optimistic read snapshot
    phase,      \* [Workers -> {"idle","reading"}] : per-worker update phase
    cap         \* runtime capacity: max workers mid-update at once

vars == << version, lastBase, snap, phase, cap >>

NumReading == Cardinality({w \in Workers : phase[w] = "reading"})

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ lastBase \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ snap \in [Workers -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ phase \in [Workers -> {"idle", "reading"}]
    /\ cap \in 1..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ lastBase = 0
    /\ snap = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [w \in Workers |-> "idle"]
    /\ cap = 1

\* A worker begins an update by snapshotting the version, if capacity allows.
Begin(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = "idle"
    /\ NumReading < cap
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![w] = version]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "reading"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, lastBase, cap >>

\* A worker commits only if its snapshot is still current.
Commit(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = "reading"
    /\ snap[w] = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ lastBase' = snap[w]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << snap, cap >>

\* A worker whose snapshot went stale abandons and will retry.
Retry(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = "reading"
    /\ snap[w] # version
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, lastBase, snap, cap >>

\* Runtime capacity changes.
RaiseCap ==
    /\ cap < MaxCap
    /\ cap' = cap + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, lastBase, snap, phase >>

LowerCap ==
    /\ cap > 1
    /\ cap' = cap - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, lastBase, snap, phase >>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Begin(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Commit(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Retry(w)
    \/ RaiseCap
    \/ LowerCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the most recent committed update was built on the version
\* immediately preceding it.
NoLostUpdate == (version = 0) \/ (lastBase = version - 1)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    MaxVer = 4
    MaxCap = 2

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line keeps a single shared program record -- the active wash recipe -- that crew workers update under optimistic locking with retry. The record carries a version number. A worker begins an update by reading the current version into a private snapshot; the number of workers allowed to be mid-update at once is capped by a runtime capacity that supervisors can raise or lower as the line load changes. A worker commits its update only if its snapshot still equals the record's live version; committing advances the version by one and remembers the snapshot the update was built on, then the worker goes idle. If a worker's snapshot has gone stale because someone else committed first, it abandons and retries, going idle to read again later. Because workers race and only one snapshot can be current, the safety concern is that no update is ever lost: every committed update is built on the version immediately preceding it, so no committed write silently overwrites and discards another worker's update. The snapshot-still-current guard on commit is what prevents lost updates.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed update to the program record is built on the version immediately preceding it, so no update is overwritten and lost.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m4p4t1 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Flights, Cap

VARIABLES
    net,        \* set of flights with an in-flight landing request (reorderable)
    qlen,       \* current holding-queue length
    mode,       \* "run" | "paused" : backpressure state
    peak        \* high-water mark of the queue length

vars == << net, qlen, mode, peak >>

Max2(a, b) == IF a > b THEN a ELSE b

TypeOK ==
    /\ net \subseteq Flights
    /\ qlen \in 0..(Cap + 2)
    /\ mode \in {"run", "paused"}
    /\ peak \in 0..(Cap + 2)

Init ==
    /\ net = {}
    /\ qlen = 0
    /\ mode = "run"
    /\ peak = 0

\* A flight sends a landing request onto the reordering network.
Request(f) ==
    /\ f \notin net
    /\ net' = net \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED << qlen, mode, peak >>

\* A request is admitted to the queue only in run mode and below capacity.
Admit(f) ==
    /\ f \in net
    /\ mode = "run"
    /\ qlen < Cap
    /\ qlen' = qlen + 1
    /\ peak' = Max2(peak, qlen + 1)
    /\ net' = net \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED mode

\* A queued flight departs as a runway frees up.
Depart ==
    /\ qlen > 0
    /\ qlen' = qlen - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << net, mode, peak >>

\* Backpressure: pause admissions when the queue reaches capacity.
Pause ==
    /\ qlen >= Cap
    /\ mode = "run"
    /\ mode' = "paused"
    /\ UNCHANGED << net, qlen, peak >>

\* Resume admissions once the queue has drained below capacity.
Resume ==
    /\ qlen < Cap
    /\ mode = "paused"
    /\ mode' = "run"
    /\ UNCHANGED << net, qlen, peak >>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Request(f)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Admit(f)
    \/ Depart
    \/ Pause
    \/ Resume

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: neither the queue length nor its high-water mark ever
\* exceeds the fixed capacity.
CapacityNeverExceeded == (qlen <= Cap) /\ (peak <= Cap)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Flights = {f1, f2, f3}
    Cap = 2

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT CapacityNeverExceeded
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator buffers inbound landing requests in a bounded holding queue before assigning runways. Flights send landing requests over the network, which may deliver them out of order, so requests sit in an in-flight set awaiting admission in arbitrary order. The allocator admits a request into the holding queue only while it is in run mode and the queue is below its fixed capacity; admission raises the queue length and also updates a high-water mark of the deepest the queue has ever been. Queued flights depart the queue as runways free up, lowering the queue length. Backpressure is expressed through mode: when the queue reaches capacity the allocator pauses admissions, and it resumes only once the queue has drained below capacity again. A flight whose request has been consumed may later send a fresh request. No matter how requests arrive and are reordered, how admissions and departures interleave, or how the allocator pauses and resumes, the safety concern is that the holding queue's length must never exceed its fixed capacity. The below-capacity guard on admission is what enforces the bound.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The holding queue's length, and its high-water mark, never exceed the fixed queue capacity.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m0p0t0 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxVer

VARIABLES
    owner,      \* current owner of the shed switch, or "none"
    inCS,       \* [Nodes -> BOOLEAN] : whether each node is operating the switch
    version,    \* lock version of the switch
    snap,       \* [Nodes -> Nat] : each node's optimistic version snapshot
    crashed     \* set of nodes that have crashed silently

vars == << owner, inCS, version, snap, crashed >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Nodes \cup {"none"}
    /\ inCS \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ snap \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Nodes

Init ==
    /\ owner = "none"
    /\ inCS = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ snap = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}

\* A live node optimistically reads the switch's current version.
Read(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![n] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, inCS, version, crashed >>

\* A seize succeeds only if the version is unchanged and the switch is unowned.
Seize(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ version = snap[n]
    /\ owner = "none"
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = n
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << snap, crashed >>

\* A node whose snapshot went stale re-reads and retries.
Retry(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ version # snap[n]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![n] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, inCS, version, crashed >>

\* A live node releases the switch.
Release(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ inCS[n]
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ owner' = "none"
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << snap, crashed >>

\* At most one node crashes silently and then takes no further action.
Crash(n) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, inCS, version, snap >>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Read(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Seize(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Retry(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Release(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion: any node operating the switch must be the single owner, so
\* two nodes are never operating it at once.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A n \in Nodes : inCS[n] => (owner = n)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
    MaxVer = 4

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A power-grid load shedder guards a single critical shed switch that must be operated by at most one control node at a time. Control nodes coordinate access with optimistic locking and retry. A node first reads the switch's lock version into a private snapshot, then optimistically tries to seize the switch. Seizing succeeds only if the version still equals the node's snapshot and the switch is currently unowned; a successful seize marks that node as owner, puts it in the operating section, and bumps the version so every other node's snapshot is now stale. A node with a stale snapshot re-reads the version and retries. A node releases the switch, clearing ownership and bumping the version again. One control node may crash silently: it simply stops taking any action from then on. If the crashed node happened to hold the switch, the switch stays owned by it and no other node can seize it -- which is safe, since the point is strict mutual exclusion. The safety concern is that the shed switch is never operated by two nodes at once. The unowned-and-version-matched guard on seizing is what preserves mutual exclusion.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The critical shed switch is never operated by more than one control node at a time.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m2p4t3 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, Gatekeeper, Cap

VARIABLES
    spool,      \* number of jobs currently in the shared spool
    vote,       \* [Participants -> {"none","yes","no"}] : votes this round
    phase,      \* "idle" | "voting" | "committed" | "aborted"
    slow        \* set of participants currently slow (deferring)

vars == << spool, vote, phase, slow >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ spool \in 0..(Cap + 2)
    /\ vote \in [Participants -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}
    /\ slow \subseteq Participants

Init ==
    /\ spool = 0
    /\ vote = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ slow = {}

\* The coordinator opens a new voting round.
Start ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ vote' = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << spool, slow >>

\* A responsive participant votes yes; the gatekeeper only if the spool has room.
VoteYes(p) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ p \notin slow
    /\ vote[p] = "none"
    /\ (p = Gatekeeper => spool < Cap)
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![p] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << spool, phase, slow >>

\* A responsive participant votes no.
VoteNo(p) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ p \notin slow
    /\ vote[p] = "none"
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![p] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << spool, phase, slow >>

\* A participant becomes slow or catches up -- it never fails outright.
BecomeSlow(p) ==
    /\ p \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED << spool, vote, phase >>

CatchUp(p) ==
    /\ p \in slow
    /\ slow' = slow \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED << spool, vote, phase >>

\* Unanimous yes commits the round: one job enters the spool.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A p \in Participants : vote[p] = "yes"
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ spool' = spool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << vote, slow >>

\* Any no vote aborts the round.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E p \in Participants : vote[p] = "no"
    /\ phase' = "aborted"
    /\ UNCHANGED << spool, vote, slow >>

\* The coordinator recycles to start the next round.
Recycle ==
    /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED << spool, vote, slow >>

\* A finished job drains from the spool.
Drain ==
    /\ spool > 0
    /\ spool' = spool - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << vote, phase, slow >>

Next ==
    \/ Start
    \/ \E p \in Participants : VoteYes(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : VoteNo(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : BecomeSlow(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : CatchUp(p)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Recycle
    \/ Drain

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: the spool's job count never exceeds its fixed capacity.
SpoolWithinCapacity == spool <= Cap

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Participants = {p1, p2, p3}
    Gatekeeper = p1
    Cap = 2

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT SpoolWithinCapacity
nl:
A print-shop job spooler admits print jobs into a shared spool of bounded capacity, and each admission is agreed by two-phase commit across several participants (the spooler, the printer, and billing). To admit a job the coordinator opens a voting round; participants each vote yes or no. One participant, the printer, acts as the capacity gatekeeper: it votes yes only if the spool currently has room below capacity, while the other participants vote yes unconditionally. If every participant votes yes the round commits and one job is added to the spool; if any votes no the round aborts. After a round ends the coordinator recycles to start the next one. Jobs also drain from the spool as they finish printing. A participant may be slow -- deferring its vote for a while and catching up later -- but it never fails outright, so every participant eventually votes. Because the printer withholds its yes when the spool is full, and a commit needs unanimous yes, the safety concern is that the spool's job count never exceeds its fixed capacity, no matter how rounds interleave with draining and slow participants. The gatekeeper's capacity-conditioned vote, gating a unanimous commit, is what enforces the bound.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of jobs in the spool never exceeds its fixed capacity.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m9p0t5 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES
    epoch,      \* current configuration epoch
    master,     \* the designated master controller, or "none"
    masterEpoch,\* epoch under which the current master was designated
    active      \* [Controllers -> BOOLEAN] : who is operating as master

vars == << epoch, master, masterEpoch, active >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ master \in Controllers \cup {"none"}
    /\ masterEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ active \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ master = "none"
    /\ masterEpoch = 0
    /\ active = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]

\* Reconfiguration bumps the epoch, vacates the master, and stands everyone down.
Reconfig ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ master' = "none"
    /\ active' = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED masterEpoch

\* Designate a master while the role is vacant, stamped with the current epoch.
Designate(c) ==
    /\ master = "none"
    /\ master' = c
    /\ masterEpoch' = epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, active >>

\* Only the current master, designated in the current epoch, may activate.
Activate(c) ==
    /\ master = c
    /\ masterEpoch = epoch
    /\ ~active[c]
    /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, master, masterEpoch >>

\* A master stops operating.
Deactivate(c) ==
    /\ active[c]
    /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, master, masterEpoch >>

\* The administrator forces one controller to be the sole active master.
AdminForce(c) ==
    /\ master' = c
    /\ masterEpoch' = epoch
    /\ active' = [x \in Controllers |-> x = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Next ==
    \/ Reconfig
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Designate(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Activate(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Deactivate(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : AdminForce(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion: any active master is the current master under the current
\* epoch, so at most one controller is ever active at a time.
MasterMutualExclusion ==
    \A c \in Controllers :
        active[c] => (master = c /\ masterEpoch = epoch)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    MaxEpoch = 3

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT MasterMutualExclusion
nl:
A power-grid load shedder must have at most one active master controller operating the grid's critical shedding authority at any time. Leadership is managed by epoch-numbered reconfiguration: each time the system reconfigures it bumps the epoch, vacates the master role, and stands down every controller that was operating. Within the current epoch a controller may be designated master while the role is vacant, stamped with the current epoch. A designated master may then activate -- begin operating the shedding authority -- but only if it is the current master and its designation carries the current epoch, so a controller holding only a stale designation from an earlier epoch cannot activate. A master deactivates when it stops operating. A privileged grid administrator may override and force any controller to be the sole active master immediately, standing down everyone else and stamping the forced master with the current epoch. The strict safety concern is mutual exclusion of the critical shedding authority: no two controllers are ever active masters at once, and no controller operates under a stale epoch. The current-master-and-current-epoch guard on activation is what preserves this.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one controller is ever the active master, and any active master is the current master under the current epoch.
